id: 314-君士坦丁大帝與李錫尼的戰爭
theater: 潘諾尼亞下省錫巴拉戰場

battle.name: 君士坦丁大帝與李錫尼的戰爭
battle.theater: 潘諾尼亞下省錫巴拉戰場
battle.brief: 公元三一四年十月五日，東方皇帝李錫尼率大軍進軍色雷斯，在潘諾尼亞下省錫巴拉與君士坦丁大帝正面對撞，是四帝共治瓦解後東西兩位奧古斯都決戰的起點。卡面亞述長矛屬西元前九世紀兩河流域的短柄長刃，與本役相隔一千兩百年，不在此役現場；當時決定勝負的是羅馬軍的方盾、飛槍、短劍與翼側騎兵。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 這場戰爭是羅馬帝國在戴克里先「四帝共治」瓦解之後，由東西兩位正帝國皇帝——西方的君士坦丁與東方的李錫尼——在巴爾幹半島與小亞細亞之間進行的第二次羅馬內戰，時在公元三一四至三一七年，即通稱「君士坦丁與李錫尼之戰」的那一輪交鋒。君士坦丁一方以戴克里先共治體系的西方軍系為底子：執政官級的宮廷禁衛軍（scholae palatinae）、從邊軍與都城駐軍抽調的野戰軍（comitatenses），以及各老兵團抽調所成的常駐分遣隊（vexillationes，即後來的「不解散」軍團），全由皇帝直接統率，他以特里爾、奈蘇斯與西爾米烏姆為本部，遙控不列顛、高盧與西班牙的防線。東方的李錫尼掌握戴克里先晚年劃給加里俄的整個東方：亞細亞、敘利亞、巴勒斯坦與埃及，行省總督（praefecti）、各軍區指揮官（praepositi）與由東方殘存軍團拼成的野戰軍，由他本人、其子瓦勒里烏斯（Valerius）以及一批出身舊元老與騎士階層的將領指揮。雙方都不是「國家對國家」，而是同一個帝國的兩半，徵兵、軍餉、裝備與訓練幾乎一致；真正的差別在地圖：君士坦丁握有多瑙河與萊茵河的戰線，以及高盧、西班牙、不列顛這些出產兵員卻財政困窘的省份；李錫尼握有東地中海的富庶行省、黑海穀道與埃及敘利亞的關稅，並能從多瑙河外、薩爾馬提亞草原與波斯邊境的小邦取得進貢和傭兵。真正把兩軍推上戰場的是「色爾底加條約」劃出的界線——東方越過哈爾斯河、占盡色雷斯與馬其頓，把君士坦丁的行政中心擠回亞得里亞海一側。
countriesEn: This war was the second round of Roman civil war fought between the two emperors of the Eastern and Western halves of the Roman Empire — Constantine in the West and Licinius in the East — across the Balkans and Asia Minor between AD 314 and AD 317, the round of fighting generally called the war of Constantine and Licinius. Constantine's side grew out of the western half of Diocletian's Tetrarchy: the praetorian guard cohorts (scholae palatinae), the mobile field army (comitatenses) drawn from the frontier garrisons and from the capital, and the standing detachments (vexillationes, the units that would become the 'indestructible' legions) formed out of the old legionary forces, all under the emperor's own command; Constantine used Trier, Naissus and Sirmium as his headquarters and controlled the defences of Britain, Gaul and Spain from there. Licinius held the whole of the east that Diocletian had assigned to Galerius — Asia Minor, Syria, Palestine and Egypt — with its praetorian prefects, the duces of the military districts and field armies assembled out of the fragmentary legions of the east, commanded by himself, by his son Valerius, and by officers drawn from the old senatorial and equestrian orders. Neither side was a state facing a foreign state: the two were halves of a single empire, with almost identical recruiting, pay, equipment and training. The real difference lay in the map. Constantine held the Danube and Rhine lines together with Gaul, Spain and Britain, rich in recruits but poor in revenue; Licinius held the wealthy provinces of the eastern Mediterranean, the Black Sea grain routes and the customs income of Egypt and Syria, and drew subsidies and auxiliaries from the client peoples beyond the Danube, from the Sarmatian steppe and from the Persian frontier. What actually set the two armies in motion was the line drawn at Serdica: the eastern share had crossed the Haemus, taken Thrace and Macedonia, and pushed Constantine's administrative centre back to the Adriatic.
people: 君士坦丁大帝（約公元二七二年生）本名弗拉維烏斯·瓦列里烏斯·君士坦丁努斯，父君士坦丁一世·克洛魯斯是戴克里先最倚重的將領之一，他本人則在軍旅中長成：公元三〇六年在約克被部下推舉為凱撒，隨後以共治者的身份進入四帝體系，三一〇年馬克西米安在阿奎萊亞被處死後，他成為西方無人可以質疑的君主；三一三年十月二八日在米爾維安橋擊敗馬克森提烏斯之後，帝國之中只剩下他與李錫尼兩位奧古斯都。李錫尼（約公元二六三年生）出身寒門，與加里俄既是同鄉又是舊友，公元二九三年前後由加里俄提拔為凱撒並以婚事接入皇室，三〇八年升為奧古斯都，是四帝共治末期東方最擅權勢的君主，也是東方宮廷所在的尼科米底亞的主人。次一代同樣要緊：君士坦丁的長子克里普斯（Crispus）早年奉命鎮壓高盧與不列顛的叛亂、熟悉軍旅，公元三一四年這一輪戰爭中曾在戰場被俘，次年獲釋，三一七年更率羅馬艦隊在赫勒斯滂海峽擊潰李錫尼的東軍艦隊，把制海權交到父親手上；他弟弟康斯坦斯（Constans）此時尚在幼年，三二一年後才被派往高盧與不列顛。文獻方面，五世紀的佐西莫斯（Zosimus）《新史》是這一輪戰爭最詳細的敘述者，今日研究者的重建大半依賴他；此外有凱撒的傳教士埃烏塞比烏斯（Eusebius of Caesarea）的《君士坦丁傳》，以及四世紀的短史家奧勒留斯·維克托與歐屈羅普斯。埃烏塞比烏斯站在勝方書寫，把整場戰爭寫成「天佑正統」的敘事，讀者需自行扣除這一層偏重。
peopleEn: Constantine the Great (born about AD 272) was born Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the son of Constantius Chlorus, one of Diocletian's most trusted commanders, and he himself grew up in the camps: in 306 he was acclaimed Caesar by his troops at York and entered the Tetrarchy as a partner, and when Maximian was executed at Aquileia in 310 on his own orders Constantine became the unchallenged ruler of the west. After the victory over Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge on 28 October 313, only two Augusti remained in the empire: himself and Licinius. Licinius (born about AD 263) came from obscure family origins and was an old friend and fellow townsman of Galerius, who raised him to the rank of Caesar around 293 and married him into the imperial family; he became Augustus in 308 and, as sole ruler of the east, he held Nicomedia with the residence of the eastern court, the revenues and the armies of the old provinces. The next generation mattered just as much. Constantine's eldest son Crispus had been used to settle unrest in Gaul and Britain and had his command experience there; he was taken prisoner in the fighting of 314, released the following year, and in 317 commanded the Roman fleet at the Hellespont, where he destroyed the eastern squadron of Licinius and handed the command of the sea to his father. His brother Constans was still a child in 314 and was sent to Gaul and Britain only after 321. As for the written record, the detailed narrative of this round of war comes from Zosimus' New History in the fifth century, on whom most modern reconstructions depend, and it is supplemented by Eusebius of Caesarea's Life of Constantine, by the short histories of Aurelius Victor and by Eutropius. Eusebius wrote from inside the winning camp and framed the whole campaign as a providence that favours the legitimate ruler, a layer of interpretation the reader has to discount.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長矛出自西元前九世紀的兩河流域，是亞述王國步兵用來壓制城防的標準配備：短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃與尾鐓，通長不足兩公尺，靠齊射與盾牆配合使用。它在本役並不現身——羅馬帝國與亞述王國之間相隔一千兩百餘年，中間還隔著希臘、羅馬、帕提亞、薩珊幾個時代，冶金傳統與武器形制早已多次改易，這件兵器不可能出現在公元三一四年的潘諾尼亞戰場上。它的價值在於作為「短柄、長刃、鐵鏃」這一類早期近戰刺擊武器的樣本，正好用來對照真正決定三一四年那一戰勝負的裝備。羅馬帝國此時的步兵骨幹是：早期矩形的 scutum 大盾，木胎包革再加金屬包邊，覆蓋前身至膝；約半米長的雙刃 gladius 短劍，佩在腰帶的劍袋（balteus）上，旁邊掛雙刃刺（pugio）；加圖改革後定為軍團標準武器的飛槍（pilum），槍桿約兩公尺、配六角形鐵質槍頭，軍團以整列齊射消耗敵陣再向前推進；近戰用的 hasta 與較重的 spatha 長劍；還有西元三世紀末仍大批裝備在身的環片鎧甲（lorica segmentata）與鎖子鎧甲（lorica hamata）。騎兵使用圓盾 parma、長矛與較短的劍，東方的重裝騎兵（如穿 clibanus 甲的騎士）連人帶馬都覆以鎖子甲與鱗甲。軍械方面有扭索式投石砲（onager）、弩砲（ballista）、攻城塔、壕溝器材與地道工具；後勤靠雙輪大車、牛車與馱騸組成的車隊，海上則有運兵的帆船與吃水淺的平底駁船。公元三一七年圍攻君士坦丁堡時，投石機與弩砲被用來對付城頭與城樓，這已是羅馬圍城技術的頂點時期。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear shown on the card belongs to ninth-century BC Mesopotamia, where it was the standard infantry weapon of the Assyrian kings: a short haft, a long blade, a socketed iron head and a butt spike, under two metres long, used in volleys in support of the shield wall. It was not present in this campaign. More than twelve centuries and several civilisations — Greek, Roman, Parthian, Sasanian — separate the Assyrian state from the Roman Empire, and the metallurgical traditions and weapon forms were remade many times over, so this object could not have stood on a Pannonian field in AD 314. Its value on the card is as a specimen of the early thrusting weapon, a short haft with a long blade and an iron head, which makes it a useful foil for the equipment that actually decided the fighting of 314. The infantry backbone of the Roman army in AD 314 was the large curved rectangular scutum, a wooden shield faced with metal and edged in bronze, reaching from the chest to the knees; the gladius, a double-edged sword of about sixty centimetres, carried in a balteus on the belt together with the pugio; the pilum, the heavy throwing javelin, roughly two metres long with a faceted iron head, fired in volley to break up an enemy formation before the charge, with the hasta and the longer spatha for close work; and, still worn in large numbers at the end of the third century, the segmentata and the mail armour. The cavalry fought with the small round parma, the spear and a shorter sword, while the eastern heavy horse, the clibanus, wore mail and scale over the animal as well as the rider. The ordnance train carried torsion onager and ballista, with siege towers, ditching tools and mining gear; the logistics ran on two-wheeled carts, ox-drawn wagons and mule trains, and on the sea on a fleet of transport sailing ships and flat-bottomed lighters. The siege of Constantinople in 317 used stone-throwing artillery and bolt-shooters against the wall circuits, and that is the high point of late Roman siegecraft.
tactics: 三一四年十月五日的錫巴拉之戰，是羅馬晚期野戰術的一次高強度樣本。開戰之前，佐西莫斯記錄雙方在開闊的潘諾尼亞平原上展開：羅馬軍以密集縱隊與分隊間隔配置，步兵在盾牆後以三列縱深站立，前列以飛槍齊射消耗敵陣，然後在號角聲中以整齊步點向前推移，盾牌相接形成連續的保護面；重裝步兵與弓箭手混編，翼側則是密集的騎兵——這是此時羅馬野戰軍的核心衝擊力量，東西雙方都把最好的騎兵放在兩翼。李錫尼以人數優勢企圖以右翼壓倒君士坦丁的中軍，戰局一度糾纏；入夜之後風雨交加，兩軍在黑暗與泥濘中繼續廝殺到深夜，中央地帶最後打成互相穿插的混戰，兩側都有整段陣線崩潰的記錄。羅馬軍在夜裡靠號令與器械維持陣線，李錫尼的中軍在潰散中由親兵掩護撤退，君士坦丁本人也在侍從掩護下才脫離戰場，於是有了「大軍往往在一支弓矢的距離內被全滅」的評價。追擊與收編是決定戰局的最後一步：李錫尼的殘部與被擄的將士成為君士坦丁手中的抵押品，隨後的色爾底加條約即以這些人與地界為交換。公元三一六年再戰時，雙方在卡帕多細亞交鋒，羅馬騎兵在遠方追擊中擊潰對手；公元三一七年，海戰成為轉折：克里普斯率艦隊在海峽狹窄處以撞角、火攻與接舷作戰，讓李錫尼的海軍無法展開，羅馬陸軍隨即進入小亞細亞，再由海路包圍君士坦丁堡，築堡封鎖、斷絕糧道，最終迫使李錫尼出降。圍城階段，工兵以攻城塔與覆蓋式通道把城牆分段處理，顯示羅馬圍城技術在四世紀初的成熟。
tacticsEn: The battle of Cibalae on 5 October 314 is a well documented example of late Roman fieldcraft at its most violent. Zosimus describes both armies deploying on the open plain of Pannonia before contact: the Romans were drawn up in a dense line with intervals between units, infantry in three lines behind the shield wall, the front rank firing pila in volley to spend the enemy's strength, then advancing in step to the sound of the horns until the shields locked into a continuous face; heavy infantry were intermingled with archers, and the cavalry massed on the wings, which by this period carried the weight of a Roman field army, both sides putting their best mounted troops on the extremities. Licinius tried to overwhelm Constantine's centre with the weight of numbers on his right, and the line see-sawed. The fighting continued into the night in wind and rain, until the centre had become a tangled melee and whole stretches of both fronts had collapsed. The Roman line was held together at night by the discipline of the trumpet and by the weight of the equipment, while Licinius' centre broke up and was covered in the retreat by his own guard; Constantine himself only extricated his person under escort, an episode that produced the judgement that armies were destroyed within bow-shot of one another. The next stage, pursuit and the taking of prisoners, decided the campaign: Licinius' broken troops and captives became Constantine's leverage, and the Treaty of Serdica was later written out of them and out of the map. In 316 the two sides met in Cappadocia, where Roman cavalry broke the enemy during the pursuit at a distance. The real turning point came in 317 at sea: Crispus fought in the narrows of the strait, using rams, fire and boarding at close range so that Licinius' fleet could never deploy, and the Roman army then crossed into Asia Minor and closed around Constantinople by sea and land, blockading it, cutting its supply, and compelling a surrender. During the blockade the engineers worked the walls section by section with towers and covered galleries, showing how mature late Roman siegecraft had become.
data: 可查的硬數字不多，且多數出自五世紀史家佐西莫斯，他的兵數常被後世判定為誇張，引用時必須打折。可確定的是幾個時間點與地理量度：錫巴拉之戰在公元三一四年十月五日，距離東西兩位皇帝全面翻臉約一年；君士坦丁自西西里渡海登陸希臘後，縱隊沿愛琴海岸北進，戰場所在的錫巴拉（今克羅地亞文科夫齊）離君士坦丁的西方首都西爾米烏姆直線約二百四十公里，離亞歷山大港的塞薩洛尼基直線約五百六十公里，離多瑙河約三百三十公里。縱深因此很短：李錫尼一旦在陸路上被逐退，東方本營與多瑙河防線之間並沒有緩衝。兵數方面，通行說法稱李錫尼集結的野戰軍在十萬以上（其中騎兵以數千計），君士坦丁一方投入的則是數萬量級的野戰軍與沿途徵召的步兵，兩者相差一倍以上；這意味著錫巴拉並非實力相等的消耗戰，而是李錫尼以人數換取戰果、卻在正面對撞中兩敗俱傷的結果。此外，赫勒斯滂海峽最窄處寬約一點二公里，公元三一七年秋的艦隊決戰即在這樣的狹窄水道內展開；史家稱東軍海上兵力達數百艘（常見說法是三百艘上下），羅馬海軍數量遠少於對手，卻由克里普斯率領，訓練與士氣佔優。全戰的結果改變了約五千平方公里的歸屬：李錫尼交出歐洲側的色雷斯、馬其頓與伊利利亞，帝國的內部分界線一路退到博斯普魯斯海峽，首都亦於公元三三〇年遷至新生的君士坦丁堡。
dataEn: Hard figures are few, and most come from the fifth-century Zosimus, whose numbers are generally judged inflated and must be discounted. What can be fixed are the dates and the measurements of distance. The battle of Cibalae was fought on 5 October 314, about a year after the two emperors fell out; after landing in Greece from Sicily, Constantine's column moved north along the coast of the Aegean. Cibala, modern Vinkovci in Croatia, lies about 240 kilometres in a straight line from Sirmium, Constantine's western capital, about 560 kilometres from Thessalonica, and about 330 kilometres from the Danube. The operational depth was therefore short: once Licinius was beaten back on the land route there was no buffer between his eastern base and the Danube line. On strength, the usual account puts Licinius' field army above 100,000 men with several thousand horse, while Constantine committed a field army of some tens of thousands, reinforced by levies from the towns on the march; the ratio was better than two to one against Constantine. Cibalae was therefore not a contest between evenly matched armies but an attempt by Licinius to buy a decision with numbers, and it ended in mutual exhaustion. The Hellespont is about 1.2 kilometres wide at its narrowest, and that is the water in which the fleets fought in the autumn of 317; the eastern fleet is described as numbering several hundred ships, commonly given as around three hundred, against a Roman fleet much smaller in number but better crewed and led. The result of the war moved roughly five thousand square kilometres of territory: Licinius gave up Thrace, Macedonia and Illyricum, and the internal frontier of the empire moved back to the Bosporus, with the capital following in AD 330 to the new Constantinople.
cause: 直接導火線是三一四年初李錫尼越過哈爾斯河、進入色雷斯的行動。背景是四帝共治在戴克里先於三〇五年退位後迅速瓦解：加里俄在與馬克森提烏斯的戰爭中耗盡元氣，於三一〇年病逝；他的同僚馬克西米安企圖復辟，兵敗後被君士坦丁在阿奎萊亞下令處死。兩位老皇帝先後清除，東西兩半便只剩下君士坦丁與李錫尼兩位奧古斯都，而且這兩位是靠政治聯姻綁在一起的姻親——君士坦丁娶了李錫尼的同父異母姊妹弗拉維婭·尤利婭·康斯坦提婭，李錫尼迎娶君士坦丁的同父異母姊妹弗拉維婭·尤利婭·海米娜，並讓自己的女兒康斯坦提婭嫁給君士坦丁的長子克里普斯。表面的分贊在公元三一〇年科隆尼亞的會談中談妥，李錫尼取得巴爾幹與色雷斯，條件是君士坦丁承認他的元首地位；到三一二年至三一三年，這一安排實際上只剩下兩個奧古斯都的名號。真正把兩人推上戰場的是四件事：其一，界線問題——李錫尼依約應以多瑙河為界，卻在塞薩盧姆擊敗馬克西米努斯·達亞後乘勢吞下色雷斯與馬其頓，並在塞薩洛尼基一帶築城設防，君士坦丁視之為對「我那一半」的越界；其二，位份問題——兩人都自稱奧古斯都，儀式上的先後、冊封的用語與書信的稱呼，成為君士坦丁不能容忍的挑釁；其三，宗教政策——李錫尼在東方收回對基督徒的寬容，拆毀教堂、沒收教產、處死教會人士，君士坦丁以基督徒皇帝自居，不能接受迫害者的名號；其四，軍功與民望——君士坦丁在米爾維安橋取勝並於三一三年冬進軍羅城，兩戰的勝利者與一支只服從一位皇帝的軍隊，對李錫尼構成最直接的威脅。於是李錫尼選擇主動出擊，試圖在對方立足未穩時將其逐回意大利。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was Licinius' crossing of the Haemus into Thrace in the early months of 314. Behind it lay the rapid disintegration of the Tetrarchy after Diocletian abdicated in 305: Galerius had spent himself in the war against Maxentius and died of illness in 310; his colleague Maximian attempted a comeback, was beaten, and was executed at Aquileia on Constantine's orders in 310. With both senior emperors removed, only Constantine and Licinius remained as Augusti, and the two were bound to each other by political marriage — Constantine had married Licinius' half-sister Flavia Julia Constantia, Licinius had married Constantine's half-sister Flavia Julia Helena, and Licinius' daughter Constantia was wedded to Constantine's eldest son Crispus. The division of power was settled at their meeting at Cologne around 310, when Licinius received the Balkans and Thrace on condition that Constantine acknowledge his own position as senior. Between 310 and 313 that arrangement came down to little more than two names. Four things pushed them to war. First, the frontier: by the terms Licinius should have held the line on the Danube, but after his victory over Maximinus Daia at Tzurulum he overran Thrace and Macedonia and began building and fortifying around Thessalonica, which Constantine read as an encroachment on his share of the empire. Second, precedence: both claimed the title of Augustus, and the order of protocol, the wording of the acclamation and the style of letters became matters Constantine could not let pass. Third, religion: Licinius withdrew toleration in the east, closed churches, confiscated property and executed clergy, and Constantine, who presented himself as a Christian emperor, could not accept the title of persecutor. Fourth, reputation and the loyalty of the army: Constantine's victory of 313 and his march on Rome that winter made him, in the eyes of the troops, the emperor of proven fortune, and that was a direct threat to the man Licinius had to outrank. So Licinius chose to attack while his opponent's position in the Balkans was still unfinished.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果把戴克里先的四帝共治徹底送進歷史，羅馬帝國重回單一皇帝統治的舊制，只是這位皇帝把首都從東方的尼科米底亞遷到博斯普魯斯海峽西岸的拜占庭，並於公元三三〇年五月十一日為它舉行祝聖典禮、正式改名君士坦丁堡。帝國的權力中心因此從多瑙河畔移到歐亞大陸的接縫，晚期羅馬的稅制、貨幣與軍隊體系都圍繞這一重心重組。軍隊層面的影響尤其深：這場戰爭是野戰軍（comitatenses）體制成熟的最後一課，宮廷禁衛軍與各軍團抽調的分遣隊被整編為常備的中央野戰力量，四十年間為君士坦丁及其後繼者提供了唯一的決策工具；李錫尼的海軍與克里普斯在海峽的勝負，則確立了晚期羅馬以海軍控制博斯普魯斯與愛琴海制海權的傳統。教會層面同樣關鍵：李錫尼的迫害使東方教會別無選擇地倒向君士坦丁，埃烏塞比烏斯得以從尼科米底亞進入皇宮，基督教會在帝國政治中的地位由此徹底改變；公元三二五年君士坦丁召開尼西亞公會議，把教義與教會秩序納入皇帝親自主持的框架，也是這場內戰勝局的直接延伸。對外則是邊疆的重新佈局：克里普斯於三一七年越過多瑙河擊退北方的哥特人，北方防線的樣式為之一變；李錫尼與波斯維持的和約則在內戰期間中斷，薩珊王國趁勢恢復對美索不達米亞與亞美尼亞的進攻，外敵趁內戰而入的風險在此後一個世紀裡反覆出現。李錫尼的名號在君士坦丁死後一度由其子孫平反，四世紀末的貶抑與除名最終仍抹去了東方的奧古斯都，帝國史從此只留一個名字。
impactEn: The result sent the Tetrarchy for good into history and restored single emperorship to the Roman state, but the emperor who did it moved the centre of gravity from the Danube to the western shore of the Bosporus: on 11 May 330 the new capital at Byzantium was dedicated and renamed Constantinople, and the fiscal, monetary and military machinery of the late empire was reorganised around that new centre. The military consequences are the most durable. This war was the last great test of the comitatentes system: the palace guard and the detachments drawn from the old legions were consolidated into a permanent central field army, which for the next forty years was the instrument of decision for Constantine and his successors. The naval dimension mattered too — Crispus' victory in the strait established the Roman tradition of controlling the Bosporus and the Aegean at sea. In the Church the consequences were equally great. Licinius' persecution forced the eastern churches into Constantine's arms, Eusebius of Caesarea moved from Nicomedia to the palace, and the position of Christianity in imperial politics was permanently altered; the Council of Nicaea summoned by Constantine in 325, which settled doctrine and church order under the emperor's own presidency, was a direct extension of the victory in this civil war. On the frontiers the war meant redrawing the map. Crispus carried the war across the Danube against the Goths in 317 and changed the pattern of the northern defence, while the peace that Licinius had kept with Persia lapsed during the civil war and the Sasanian kingdom renewed its pressure on Mesopotamia and Armenia — the risk of an external enemy taking advantage of the internal war returned again and again over the following century. The name of Licinius was briefly rehabilitated by Constantine's sons after his death, but the condemnation and the final obliteration of the eastern Augustus in the last decades of the fourth century left imperial history with a single name.
result: 三一四年十月五日的錫巴拉之戰，李錫尼大敗，君士坦丁取得巴爾幹的主動權。公元三一五年雙方在色爾底加議和，條約把歐洲側的色雷斯、馬其頓與伊利利亞劃給君士坦丁，東方的亞細亞、敘利亞與埃及仍屬李錫尼，兩人共同以奧古斯都的名義共治，並以各自兒子作為凱撒繼承人。和平維持不到一年：三一六年李錫尼再度進攻君士坦丁的勢力範圍，在卡帕多細亞的馬爾迪亞會戰敗北，退守拜占庭；公元三一七年秋，克里普斯率羅馬艦隊在赫勒斯滂海峽擊潰李錫尼的東軍艦隊，取得海峽控制權，君士坦丁隨即率軍進入小亞細亞、攻入拜占庭，李錫尼反被圍在城中，糧盡援絕，於三一七年十一月前後出降。君士坦丁以禮遇相待，把李錫尼一家安置在塞薩洛尼基的莊園裡，這是羅馬內戰史上少見的仁慈收場；但李錫尼仍於公元三二四年被處決。真正的終局發生在公元三二四年九月十八日的克律索波利斯戰役——君士坦丁在海峽對岸攻破李錫尼的陣地，奪取君士坦丁堡，俘獲李錫尼本人。從三一四年的錫巴拉算起，東西兩位奧古斯都的對峙整整延續十年，最後以其中一方被消滅、帝國重新統一於君士坦丁一人之手告終。戰役序列上的意義是：這場戰爭並沒有靠任何一次會戰定生死，真正決定它的是三一七年海峽的制海權與隨後四年的攻城消耗——這也正是晚期羅馬戰爭形態的一個縮影。
resultEn: The battle of Cibalae on 5 October 314 was a defeat for Licinius and gave Constantine the initiative in the Balkans. In 315 the two emperors made peace at Serdica: Thrace, Macedonia and Illyricum on the European side passed to Constantine, while Asia Minor, Syria and Egypt remained with Licinius; both ruled as Augusti and used their own sons as Caesars. The peace lasted barely a year. In 316 Licinius struck again into Constantine's sphere, was beaten in Cappadocia at the battle of Mardia, and fell back on Byzantium. In the autumn of 317 Crispus' Roman fleet destroyed the eastern squadron of Licinius in the Hellespont and took command of the strait; Constantine then crossed into Asia Minor and attacked Byzantium, and Licinius was invested in his own city, his supply cut and his food exhausted, until he surrendered in about November 317. Constantine received him with courtesy and settled the family at a villa near Thessalonica, one of the rare merciful endings in the history of Roman civil war; Licinius was nevertheless executed in 324. The true conclusion came at the battle of Chrysopolis, fought opposite Chalcedon on 18 September 324, when Constantine broke Licinius' position on the Asian shore, took Byzantium and captured the enemy emperor in person. From Cibalae in 314 to the end, the confrontation between the two Augusti lasted ten years and finished with one of them destroyed and the empire reunited under Constantine alone. The significance of the sequence is that the war was not decided by any single field battle: what settled it was command of the sea in 317 and the siege attrition of the four years that followed, which is itself a summary of the changing shape of warfare in the late Roman Empire.
